title: Multilingual Emergency Dispatcher Assistance
business: Emergency response centers handling high-stress, multi-language calls.
problem: Traditional text-based or sequential audio processing introduces critical latency, preventing dispatchers from understanding urgent, non-native language distress signals in real-time.
solution: The GPT-4o Realtime model enables bidirectional audio streaming via WebSockets, allowing the system to process incoming distress calls and provide immediate, low-latency conversational support or translation without the delay of separate transcription and synthesis steps.
steps: Establish a persistent WebSocket connection to the v1/realtime endpoint.
Stream raw audio packets from the emergency caller directly to the model session.
Configure the model to output audio responses that guide the caller through triage protocols.
Utilize function_calling to trigger automated dispatch alerts based on extracted location or incident data.
Monitor session health and latency metrics to ensure continuous, uninterrupted communication.
outcome: Dispatchers receive immediate, context-aware assistance, reducing the time required to assess and categorize emergency situations regardless of the caller's language.
limitation: The model's reliance on a persistent WebSocket connection means that network instability can cause audio gaps; developers must implement robust reconnection logic and monitor packet loss to ensure session reliability.
